title: kv-cache-attn-seqlen-debug-scratchpad-8
content:
Context:
- Intermittent correctness failures observed for long-context requests when runtime switches attention kernel (kv-cache enabled). Failures cluster around sequence length boundaries (~2048 / 2049, 4096 / 4097).
- Repro rate ~3-10% in smoke tests; higher when forcing specific kernel combo.
- Affects both quantized and fp16 paths, more common on A100 and RTX6000 nodes.

Recent observations (log excerpts):
- Kernel selection log (trimmed):
  INFO:seq-router:request seq_len=2049 -> selected_kernel=flash_attn_v2 (fallback:unfused_attn)
  DEBUG:kvcache:attach_kv_cache id=0 offset=2048 expected_last_index=2048 actual_last_index=2047
  ERROR:resp-gen:token_mismatch at step=12 predicted==ground_truth? false

- Runtime panic in a repro (local):
  runtime error: index out of range: slice bounds [2048:2049] with length 2048
  stack: runtime.go:423 attach_kv_cache -> cache_write.go:87

Commands I ran (to reproduce locally):
1) Baseline python repro that hits the issue ~3%:
   PYTHONPATH=./py python -m repro.scripts.kv_seqlen_repro --model gpt-medium --context 2049 --n_trials 500 --seed 42
2) Force kernel selection via env var to isolate kernel pairings:
   RUNTIME_FORCE_KERNEL=flash_attn_v2 PYTHONPATH=./py python -m repro.scripts.kv_seqlen_repro --context 2049 --n_trials 200
   -> repro rate jumped to ~30%
3) Disable kv cache as control:
   RUNTIME_DISABLE_KV_CACHE=1 python -m repro.scripts.kv_seqlen_repro --context 2049 --n_trials 500
   -> repro rate 0% (implies kv cache/attach path involved)
4) Run with verbose kv logs to capture offsets:
   RUNTIME_KV_LOG_LEVEL=debug python -m repro.scripts.kv_seqlen_repro --context 2049 --n_trials 50
   -> saw multiple lines: attach_kv_cache id=0 offset=2048 last_index=2047

Error snippets collected:
- "expected_last_index=2048 actual_last_index=2047"
- "kv cache write size mismatch: wrote 2048 bytes but offset assumed 2049"
- "index out of range: slice bounds [2048:2049] with length 2048"
- token mismatch at generation step 12 - outputs diverge after kernel switch

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Off-by-one in kv-cache offset adjustment when switching kernels that use different block sizes or fused/unfused layouts. Sequence boundary triggers a change in internal indexing.
2) Kernel handshake path neglects to flush or remap the KV index base when moving from continuous-batched path to single-request path (or vice versa).
3) Race between cache attach and first write when batching + prefix cache warming enabled -> sometimes writer uses previous request's base index.
4) Memory aliasing / view created with incorrect shape for specific quantized path -> slice bounds error. Less likely because also occurs in fp16.
5) Off-by-one in attention mask computation that only surfaces when seq_len % block_size == 1 (i.e., 2049) -> leads to mismatch in expected_last_index.

Quick checks attempted and results:
- Reproduced same failure with minimal repro harness (no batching) when forcing kernel switch before generation -> repro persists, so batching not strictly necessary.
- Disabling automatic prefix caching eliminates the error. Suggests attach_kv_cache flow (prefix attach) is implicated.
- Inserted assertion in kv cache attach: assert(last_index+1 == offset) -> triggered on failing runs.
- Reproduced on CPU-only builds? No, failures only on GPU runs, so kernel selection/path on GPU matters.

Trace of likely failing flow (notes):
1) Request arrives with prefix_len P (could be 2048).
2) Router selects kernel K1 for prefix processing -> writes KV with base index B = P.
3) For generation chunk, kernel K2 selected (different layout) -> attach_kv_cache called expecting base = P+1 (?)
4) Mismatch leads to attach_kv_cache asserting old_last_index vs new offset. Possible off-by-one when converting between token counts and internal kv buckets.

Things to inspect in code (files / symbols):
- serving-runtime/kv_cache/attach.go -> attachKVCaches / computeOffsetForKernel
- serving-runtime/attention/kernel_selector.go -> selectKernelForRequest
- serving-runtime/attention/layouts.go -> blockSizeForKernel and index mapping funcs
- serving-runtime/batching/cache_warmup.go -> prefix caching/warmup flow
- tests/unit/kv_cache_test.go -> add edge-case test for seq_len boundary (2048->2049)

Local quick patch idea (temporary guard):
- In attach_kv_cache, clamp offset to >= last_index and log + drop request if inconsistent.
- But we need root fix rather than drop. Add extra invariant checks and dump memviews when invariant violated.

Next steps (actionable):
- Add unit tests: simulate two kernels with different block sizes; assert offset translation stable for P=2047..2050. (Priya to pick up).
- Add integration test in CI that runs small stochastic harness with RUNTIME_FORCE_KERNEL permutations to catch regressions. (Ethan).
- Add more verbose dumps on failing runs: hex dump of last 64 bytes of KV store + offsets. Store to /tmp/kv-debug-<ts>. Consider S3 archival for later analysis.
- Bisect recent changes to kernel_selector and kv-cache attach (PRs in last 2 months): start from PRs 1310..1423 (likely culprits).
- Try repro on older runtime binary (2025-10 build) to see if regression introduced recently.

Notes / breadcrumbs from Slack and past runs:
- Slack thread #runtime-kv: @ethan reported similar failure on 2025-12-02 but thought it was quantization. Link: slack:/archives/C01234567/p1678901234567
- Local repro IDs: repro/2026-02-18/run-1 (attached kv logs)
- Correlation: nodes with recent NVIDIA driver 510.x had slightly higher repro rate; need to control for driver.

Temporary mitigations in prod (discussion):
- Avoid routing requests that cross seq_len boundary to kernels with different block sizes; route to conservative kernel. Risk: small perf hit but better availability.
- Disable prefix caching for customers hitting this error until fix is backported.

Open questions:
- Are we converting between token-based offsets and bucket-based offsets inconsistently? (check conversions in layouts.go)
- Does any kernel use an implicit sentinel token that shifts indexing by 1? (e.g., BOS/EOS special handling)
- Is there a path where cached KV is compacted or deduped on attach causing last_index to change?

TODO (short):
- [ ] Add unit test for seq_len boundary offsets (owner: Priya)
- [ ] Add integration CI job forcing kernel combos (owner: Ethan)
- [ ] Instrument attach_kv_cache to dump KV meta + last N bytes on failure (owner: Maya)
- [ ] Start PR bisect for kernel_selector changes (owner: Maya)
- [ ] Try repro on older 2025-10 binary (owner: Maya)

Appendix (raw useful snippets):
- repro command used for heavy run:
  RUNTIME_FORCE_KERNEL=flash_attn_v2,unfused_attn RUNTIME_KV_LOG_LEVEL=debug PYTEST_ADDOPTS= -k "kv_seqlen" python -m repro.scripts.kv_seqlen_repro --context 2049 --n_trials 2000
- Example failing kv log (full):
  [2026-02-18T14:12:03.124Z] DEBUG kvcache id=0 attach request_id=abc123 offset=2048 last_index=2047 entries=2048
  [2026-02-18T14:12:03.124Z] WARN  kvcache id=0 offset_mismatch expected=2048 actual=2047 request_id=abc123
  [2026-02-18T14:12:03.125Z] ERROR resp-gen request_id=abc123 mismatch at gen_step=12

If anyone picks this up, see linked PR for context and ping me on Slack. Will push instrument patch to feature/kv-attach-invariants branch and open PR once tests added.

End of scratchpad.
